Below: Sixteen year old Pam Friel was our top 400 metre runner of 1993, just failing to nip under the 60 second barrier.

James Ganio was impressive in winning the under-17 long jump and Pam Friel had to settle for a silver medal winning effort in the 200 metres after finding that several of the events were cancelled due to insufficient entries.

Another of our British athletes was also present - Kelly Holmes - and we soon found that we would actually be competing against her as she belongs to Middlesex Ladies. Pam Friel came up against her in the 400m and the Belgravian rose to the occasion by setting a personal best and coming 2nd.
Pam Friel was well in command in the 400m and given still conditions and a few more races under her belt looked set fair for a sub-60 clocking in the next few weeks.

There were some great shots of Colin Jackson skimming the "Sticks In My Lane" but the boys and girls starting out on the hard road to success were all young Belgravians: Milton Holder, Syreeta Stracey, Marlon Dickson, Pam Friel and James Hilston.
